attrs.evidence: lowering_check.mjs: decode-is-structural (L0(L1(A(N0,…A(N0,N1)…))) with five applications decodes to {status:'value', value:5}) and decoder-boundary-named (a non-numeral is decode-not-a-church-numeral, a compacted signature is decode-signature-compacted, and 0 and 1 decode — the two shapes that carry no dup). decode_sem_id is distinct from lowering_sem_id and asserted so.
attrs.statement: ONE CANONICAL TARGET NORMAL FORM UNDER ONE DECODER DETERMINES ONE STRUCTURAL TRVM OUTCOME, OR A STRUCTURAL DECODE REFUSAL. decode_sem_id identifies the decoder, and decoding is a THIRD relation rather than the tail of lowering: a lowering can be perfect while the decoder reads the normal form wrongly, and a decoder can be perfect while lowering emitted the wrong target term. They fail independently, so they are proved independently. The outcome is STRUCTURAL — {status:'value', value} or {status:'refused', code, locus} — never a rendered reason, which would recreate round 16's 'the identity bound a spelling' one layer up. The decoder reads the CANONICAL SIGNATURE rather than a readback string — the same bytes the 48/48 bridge has agreed on since round 12 — so it cannot be misled by a binder name. §5 compaction is irreversible, so a compacted signature is REFUSED rather than guessed at; that bounds the decodable numerals and the bound is stated rather than discovered.
